node-2.label: She observed skin discoloration on the left breast 6 months prior, which progressively increased and prompted her to seek medical attention.

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed a single 3 × 3 cm pink, non-tender, raised lesion on the left breast at the 12:00 position.

node-4.label: Medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and osteoporosis, with no previous breast health issues or surgeries.

node-5.label: She reported no associated pain, new masses, nipple discharge/retraction, or lymphadenopathy; vital signs were within normal limits, she appeared in no distress, and she tolerated a treatment procedure well without complications.

attrs.why: New pathologist analysis reports biopsy with dermal confluent large lymphoid cells, Ki-67 95%, CD3/CD4/CD5/BCL2/MUM1/CD30 positivity, and cytokeratin/ALK1/MPO negativity, explicitly excluding malignant breast neoplasm. Radiologist concurs that the CD30+ large T-cell lymphoid infiltrate favors a cutaneous lymphoproliferative disorder over breast malignancy. The prior nonspecific supports (age, progressive discoloration, pink lesion) are outweighed by the lack of epithelial malignancy markers; confidence drops from 0.45 to 0.02.

Biopsy and expert analyses reveal a primary cutaneous CD30+ large T-cell lymphoid infiltrate (CD3/CD4/CD5/BCL2/MUM1+, cytokeratin/ALK1/MPO-, Ki-67 95%, epidermal ulceration). Both pathologist and radiologist favor a primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder/lymphoma, which supports the primary cutaneous malignancy hypothesis. Localized skin presentation without systemic findings fits this category; remaining uncertainty is pcALCL vs LyP and lack of systemic staging/TCR clonality, so confidence rises from 0.35 to 0.85.

The biopsy shows confluent large lymphoid cells, epidermal ulceration, Ki-67 95%, and CD30+ T-cell lineage markers, which are not consistent with a benign skin/breast lesion. Although lymphomatoid papulosis can be indolent, it is a CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder rather than a simple benign dermatosis or breast lesion. The benign hypothesis is therefore largely refuted, with confidence reduced from 0.20 to 0.05.

node-13.label: Patient has primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL)

attrs.why: A single persistent, progressively enlarging 3 cm raised lesion over 6 months, together with confluent dermal large CD30+ T cells, BCL2/MUM1 expression, Ki-67 95%, and epidermal ulceration, is characteristic of pcALCL as a defined subtype within the CD30+ cutaneous lymphoproliferative category. However, the solitary, continuously progressive lesion over 6 months with 95% Ki-67 and ulceration is atypical for the typically recurrent, waxing-and-waning papules of LyP, and the expert analyses leave the entity unresolved. Confidence is therefore lower at 0.3 pending clonality and systemic staging.
